;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Vienna attack]]
**Four civilians are killed and 22 others injured after a gunman [[mass shooting|opens fire]] in six locations in the streets of [[Vienna]], [[Austria]], near the central [[Schwedenplatz]] square. The Interior Minister described it as a "terror attack". The attacker was shot dead, and is identified as an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic]] supporter who tried to join the group in [[Syria]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54788613 (BBC News)]
**The [[Austrian Armed Forces]] are deployed to secure public buildings in Vienna. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/vienna-shooting-live-updates-synagogue-austria-latest-b1541213.html (''The Independent'')]
**The [[Police of the Czech Republic|Czech Police Forces]] announce that they will carry out random border checks with [[Austria]] as a preventive measure against terrorism. [https://www.dw.com/en/vienna-terror-attack-islamist-motive-suspected-in-deadly-shootings/a-55478882 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[2020 Kabul University attack]]
**Three militants open fire at [[Kabul University]]'s campus, killing 22 people and wounding 22 others. The attack began around the time [[government of Afghanistan|government]] officials were expected to arrive at the campus for the opening of an [[Iran]]ian [[book fair]]. The gunmen are killed during a battle with security forces. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-54750839 (BBC News)]
*[[Operation Barkhane]]; [[Mali War]]
**[[French Armed Forces|French military]] [[airstrike]]s kill over 50 [[Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb|al-Qaeda]]-linked [[jihadist]]s in [[Mali]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/french-airstrikes-kill-over-50-212531933.html (AFP via Yahoo! News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[List of most-viewed YouTube videos|Most-viewed YouTube videos]]
**"[[Baby Shark#Pinkfong version|Baby Shark Dance]]", produced by [[Pinkfong]], surpasses "[[Despacito#Music video|Despacito]]" as the most-viewed video on [[YouTube]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/music/2020/nov/02/baby-shark-becomes-most-viewed-youtube-video-ever-beating-despacito (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Goni (2020)|Typhoon Goni]]
***The death toll in the [[Philippines]] from [[Typhoon Goni (2020)|Typhoon Goni]], the world's strongest this year, rises to 20 people. Electricity, water and phone networks are cut off in [[Catanduanes]], while homes are buried under [[volcanic rock]]s in [[Albay]]; those two are the provinces where all the deaths occurred. About one million people have been evacuated. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/2/typhoon-goni-duterte-to-inspect-damage-as-philippine-toll-rises (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Aegean Sea earthquake]]
**Twenty-eight more people are found dead under debris in [[İzmir]] after an [[earthquake]] struck [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]] three days ago, bringing the death toll to 113. The earthquake is currently the deadliest this year. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/3/turkey-earthquake-death-toll-hits-100 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Eta]] is expected to rapidly increase within the next 18 hours according to the [[National Hurricane Center]] (NHC). The storm is moving in the [[Caribbean Sea]] towards [[Nicaragua]] bringing "devastating conditions". A [[hurricane warning]] has been issued for Nicaragua and [[Honduras]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/11/02/weather/tropical-storm-eta-monday/index.html (CNN)]
*Two houses on [[Durham Place, Chelsea|Durham Place]], [[Chelsea, London]] collapse shortly before midnight, leading to around 40 people being evacuated. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/nov/03/london-street-evacuated-after-two-houses-collapse-during-building-works (''The Guardian'')]
*[[De Akkers metro station crash]]
**A train on the [[Rotterdam Metro]] crashed through the [[buffer stop]] at [[De Akkers metro station]] in the city of [[Spijkenisse]] in the [[Netherlands]]. The lead car of the train partially rested on a {{Convert|10|m||abbr=|adj=on}} high whale sculpture erected in front of the station, preventing the train from falling to the street below. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/sculpture-whales-tail-saves-train-plummeting-30-feet/story?id=73967998 (ABC News)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports a record 52,518 new infections in the past 24 hours, raising its cumulative case total to 1.46 million. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/france-52-518-new-cases-418-deaths-from-covid-19/2028563 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns]]
****[[Greece]] imposes a two-week lockdown on its second largest city of [[Thessaloniki]] to curb the spread of [[COVID-19]]. Flights to and from the city are also suspended beginning tomorrow. The lockdown also affects the northern city of [[Serres]]. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2020-11-greece-imposes-lockdown-largest-city.html (Medical Xpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Giuseppe Conte]] told Italian lawmakers he will announce new restrictions that would vary by region but would include a "late evening" curfew for many regions. Therefore, high schools across the country will move to full-time distance learning and shopping malls will close on weekends. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/europe/523981-italy-imposes-additional-coronavirus-restrictions-due-to (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo]]
****The [[Government of Kosovo|government]] imposes a curfew from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. local time for all restaurants and cafés. No more than five people are allowed to socialize, and no mass events may be held. Concerts, cultural and sporting events may be held if seating is limited. In addition, elderly people are allowed out only at certain times, and masks are mandatory outdoors. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/kosovo_has_launched_new_restrictive_measures_to_prevent_a_collapse_of_its_national_health_system-1129571/ (''The National Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] surpasses 400,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://112.international/politics/number-of-coronavirus-cases-in-ukraine-exceeds-400000-56121.html (112 UA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (country)]]
****[[Prime Minister of Georgia|Prime Minister]] [[Giorgi Gakharia]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://agenda.ge/en/news/2020/3454 (Agenda.ge)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 440 new deaths in the past 24 hours, pushing the nationwide death toll to 35,738. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1757426/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
****[[British Columbia]]'s deputy provincial health officer Réka Gustafson and [[Ministry of Health (British Columbia)|Health Minister]] [[Adrian Dix]] announce a record 1,120 new cases over the weekend, which includes 352 cases from Friday to Saturday, 389 cases were reported from Saturday to Sunday, and 379 cases from Sunday to Monday. [https://bc.ctvnews.ca/covid-19-records-shattered-as-b-c-announces-1-120-new-cases-from-the-weekend-1.5171043 (CTV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
****Rose Addo becomes the first passenger to take part in a new COVID-19 screening pilot program which landed at [[Calgary International Airport]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/calgary/covid-traveller-screening-calgary-aiport-1.5786889 (CBC)]
***The [[Government of Canada|government]] announces that from November 21, air travellers whose final destination is [[Canada]] will be required to submit their information through ArriveCAN before they board their flight and starting immediately, travellers that enter by land or marine modes are strongly encouraged to continue ArriveCAN by downloading the mobile app or signing in online to provide the mandatory information before they arrive. [https://www.biospace.com/article/releases/government-of-canada-announces-new-mandatory-requirements-for-travellers-to-canada/ (Biospace)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
****[[Governor of Massachusetts|Governor]] [[Charlie Baker]] announces new restrictions for the [[Massachusetts|state]], including a stay-at-home order, curfew for businesses, reduction of indoor gatherings, and a tighter [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]]. The restrictions will take effect on November 6. [https://boston.cbslocal.com/2020/11/02/massachusetts-coronavirus-reopening-gov-charlie-baker-covid-19-latest-news/ (WBZ-TV)] [https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/11/02/nation/charlie-baker-discuss-new-executive-orders-coronavirus-news-conference-today/ (''The Boston Globe'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indiana]]
****The first round of [[Indiana National Guard]] troops are expected to arrive at nursing homes in the [[Indiana|state]]. The move was announced by [[Governor of Indiana|Governor]] [[Eric Holcomb]] during a press conference in [[Indianapolis]] on October 28. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/ct-ptb-covid-nursing-homes-national-guard-st-1103-20201102-cj2t24t6lrfm7hfluod3eh3av4-story.html (''The Chicago Tribune'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Panama]]
***[[President of Panama|President]] [[Laurentino Cortizo]] self-isolates after a close coworker tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-panama-president/panama-president-isolating-after-coworker-tests-positive-for-covid-19-idUSKBN27J045 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[South Africa]]n [[pharmaceutical company]] [[Aspen Pharmacare]] announces that they have made a deal with [[Johnson & Johnson]] to manufacture their COVID-19 vaccine candidate if approved in South Africa and internationally. [https://www.startribune.com/south-african-firm-and-johnson-johnson-strike-vaccine-deal/572948832/ (''The Star Tribune'')] 

;International relations
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**Former [[National Security Agency]] contractor [[Edward Snowden]] applies for [[Russian citizenship]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/11/02/europe/edward-snowden-russian-citizenship-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020 Tanzanian general election]]
**Police arrest opposition activists [[Freeman Mbowe]], [[Godbless Lema]], [[Isaya Mwita Charles]] and Boniface Jacob ahead of planned protests against the election which gave incumbent [[John Magufuli]] another term. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/2/tanzania-police-arrest-opposition-party-leader-ahead-of-protests (Al Jazeera)]
*''[[Depp v News Group Newspapers Ltd]]''
**The [[High Court of Justice]] finds in favour of [[News UK]] in the [[libel]] action that [[Johnny Depp]] took against them over claims he had beaten his [[ex (relationship)|ex]]-wife [[Amber Heard]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2020/nov/02/johnny-depp-loses-libel-case-against-sun-over-claims-he-beat-ex-wife-amber-heard (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Government of France|French government]] announces that it will ban the [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[Ultranationalism|ultranationalist]] group [[Grey Wolves (organization)|Grey Wolves]]. [[Minister of the Interior (France)|Interior Minister]] [[Gerald Darmanin]] describes the group as "particularly aggressive" and will be seeking its dissolution. The group has been accused of vandalizing [[Armenian Genocide]] memorials, including one in [[Lyon]] last weekend. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/2/france-to-ban-turkish-ultra-nationalist-grey-wolves-group (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Algerian constitutional referendum]]
**The proposed amendmends to the [[Constitution of Algeria]] are passed with over 66% of the votes having been cast in favour. Voting turnout however was at a record low of less than 24%. [https://www.dw.com/en/algeria-passes-constitutional-changes-after-historically-low-turnout/a-55473708 (DW)]
*[[2020 Moldovan presidential election]]
**[[Maia Sandu]] wins the first election round of [[Moldova]]'s latest presidential election by gaining around 36% of the votes. Incumbent [[President of Moldova|president]] [[Igor Dodon]] received over 32%  and will face Sandu in the second round later in November. [https://www.dw.com/en/moldova-election-heads-for-runoff-opposition-secures-narrow-lead/a-55468282 (DW)]
